correctness.rationale: For uniform volume on the origin Voronoi cell the squared gap is the minimum of ||v||²−2⟨x,v⟩ over nonzero sites. Ties at the cell boundary do not affect the probability. The ± shortest inequalities force the endpoint λ and at positive ε make the E-coordinate lie in εK. The event volume equals that of the closed shifted halfspace intersection, with denominator det Λ; for ε>0 near zero this intersection contains an open neighborhood of zero. For a nonrelevant v, the midpoint criterion gives a split v=a+b into strictly shorter nonzero vectors with ⟨a,b⟩≥0. The two shorter inequalities displaced by t=λ−ε imply the v inequality at the same t≥0, so length induction reduces to finitely many relevant vectors and retains all shortest ones. After x=εz+y, the bounded z lies in K and the finitely many other constraints on y differ from those of H by O(ε) uniformly in z. The positive nonshort offsets allow each section to be squeezed between (1−cε)H and (1+cε)H; H is bounded inside V and has a relative origin neighborhood. The Jacobian is ε^r, proving the coefficient and next-order bound, also when H is zero-dimensional. The finite prospective vertices depend affinely on ε; feasibility and active equalities stabilize on a sufficiently small positive interval. A fixed pulling triangulation gives the exact degree-≤d volume polynomial. In full shortest span the nonshort constraints are slack on εK, so that polynomial is a monomial. For the first planar example the only nonshort strip pair active at ε=0 is from ±(2/5,6/5); the local area is ε(3/5+ε)/(6/5), divided by covolume 6/5, giving both stated coefficients. For the second, the two unit vectors give a strip intersection of area 13/12 and covolume 12/13. The orthogonal product follows from the coordinate strip widths.
residual_risks: The exact endpoint polynomial is local; symbolic calculations, not the finite checker, establish the claim for arbitrary full-rank lattices.

evidence: Koçak–Ratiu show ordinary Euclidean inner-tube volume is piecewise polynomial. McKilliam–Grant–Clarkson give the relevant-vector halfspaces. The gap shifts all unnormalized inequalities by the same amount; in Euclidean normal distance these are length-dependent rates.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Polynomial behavior for ordinary Euclidean offsets alone neither treats the gap erosion in general nor identifies the lowest power with a shortest-vector span and its coefficient. The known halfspace description and general polytope tools are ingredients.

originality.rationale: The supported increment is that this particular squared runner-up margin intrinsically recovers the real span dimension of the shortest vectors in every dimension, with a positive mixed-dimensional coefficient. Voronoi facet geometry, the definition of well-roundedness and generic inner-volume polynomiality are not claimed as new. The strongest same-statistic match gives a full special-family law and a general planar asymptotic at the opposite endpoint, not the arbitrary-dimensional upper-endpoint claim.
residual_risks: The bounded search does not exclude an unindexed anisotropic inner-erosion theorem or a closer antecedent in the lattice-decoding literature.

value.rationale: For a natural population margin, the formula recovers the dimension of a geometric invariant without being given the shortest vectors, and tests well-roundedness in known dimension. It relates this recovery to an explicit coefficient depending on transverse geometry. The two nonorthogonal examples show the rank effect is not an artifact of Cartesian products.
residual_risks: No guarantee of reliable finite-sample recovery or complete lattice identification is asserted.
